title.raw: 卷144 志一百十九 刑法三

sentences.zh: 志一百十九

translations.literal: Treatise 119.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 119

sentences.zh: 刑法三

translations.literal: Penal Law 3.
translations.idiomatic: Penal Law 3

sentences.zh: 太祖始創八旗，每旗設總管大臣一，佐管大臣二。

translations.literal: The Taizu first created the Eight Banners; each banner was provided one supervising minister and two assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu first established the Eight Banners, he appointed one supervising minister and two assisting ministers for each banner.

sentences.zh: 又置理政聽訟大臣五人，號為議政五大臣。

translations.literal: He also appointed five ministers to manage government and hear lawsuits, styled the Five Great Deliberative Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up five ministers charged with governance and adjudication, known as the Five Great Deliberative Ministers.

sentences.zh: 扎爾固齊十人，號為理事十大臣。

translations.literal: Ten jaruči were appointed, styled the Ten Great Administrative Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Ten jaruči officials were named the Ten Great Administrative Ministers.

sentences.zh: 凡聽斷之事，先經扎爾固齊十人審問，然後言於五臣，五臣再加審問，然後言於諸貝勒。

translations.literal: For all matters heard and decided, they first passed through examination by the ten jaruči, then were reported to the five ministers, who examined them again, and then were reported to the various beile.
translations.idiomatic: Every case to be adjudicated was first examined by the ten jaruči, then reported to the five ministers for a second review, and only then brought before the beile.

sentences.zh: 眾議既定，猶恐冤抑，親加鞫問。

translations.literal: Once the collective deliberation was settled, fearing still that injustice might be suppressed, he personally added interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the collective decision was reached, he still feared wrongful conviction and personally conducted further interrogation.

sentences.zh: 天命元年，諭貝勒大臣曰：「國人有事，當訴於公所，毋得訴於諸臣之家。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianming, he instructed the beile and ministers: "When the people of the state have affairs, they should lodge suits at the public office and must not lodge suits at the homes of various ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianming, he instructed the beile and ministers: "When subjects of the state have grievances, they must bring them to the public tribunal and may not plead them at any minister's private residence.

sentences.zh: 茲播告國中，自貝勒大臣以下有罪，當靜聽公斷，執拗不服者，加等治罪。

translations.literal: Now this is proclaimed throughout the state: from beile and ministers downward, if guilty, they should quietly accept public judgment; those stubborn and refusing to submit shall be punished by increased degrees.
translations.idiomatic: This proclamation was now broadcast throughout the realm: from the beile and ministers downward, anyone found guilty must accept the public verdict in silence; those who stubbornly refused would be punished one degree more severely.

sentences.zh: 凡事俱五日一聽斷於公所，其私訴於家，不執送而私斷者，治罪不貸。」

translations.literal: All affairs alike were to be heard and decided at the public office once every five days; those who privately pleaded at home, or who did not deliver the parties but privately judged, were punished without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: All cases were to be heard at the public tribunal every five days. Anyone who accepted private suits at home, or who adjudicated on his own without delivering the parties to the public office, would be punished without mercy."

sentences.zh: 十一年，太宗以議政五大臣、理事十大臣不皆分授，或即以總管、佐管兼之，於是集諸貝勒定議裁撤。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the Taizong, because the Five Great Deliberative Ministers and Ten Great Administrative Ministers were not all separately appointed—some holding the posts of supervising or assisting ministers concurrently—thereupon assembled the various beile to deliberate and decided to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, the Taizong found that the Five Great Deliberative Ministers and Ten Great Administrative Ministers were not always separately appointed—some men held those posts concurrently with banner supervising or assisting duties—so he convened the beile, who resolved to abolish the offices.

sentences.zh: 每旗由佐管大臣審斷詞訟，不令出兵駐防。

translations.literal: Each banner was to have its assisting ministers try lawsuits, and they were not permitted to go out on campaign or garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner's assisting ministers were to adjudicate civil suits, and they were barred from fielding troops for campaigns or garrison service.

sentences.zh: 其每旗別設調遣大臣二員，遇有駐防調遣所屬詞訟，仍令審理。

translations.literal: For each banner two dispatch ministers were separately established; when garrison or dispatch duties gave rise to lawsuits within their jurisdiction, they were still ordered to try them.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner was also given two dispatch ministers; whenever lawsuits arose among men under their garrison or dispatch command, those ministers were still to hear the cases.

sentences.zh: 天聰七年，設刑部承政、參政、啟心郎等官，聽訟始有專責。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tiancong, the Ministry of Justice posts of chengzheng, canzheng, qixinlang, and the like were established, and hearing lawsuits first had dedicated responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tiancong, the Ministry of Justice was staffed with chengzheng, canzheng, qixinlang, and related posts, giving litigation a dedicated bureaucracy for the first time.

sentences.zh: 世祖入主中夏，仍明舊制，凡訴訟在外由州縣層遞至於督撫，在內歸總於三法司。

translations.literal: When the Shizu entered and ruled the Central Plains, he still followed the Ming old system: all lawsuits outside passed layer by layer from prefecture and county up to governor-general and governor; inside, all were gathered under the Three Judicial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu took possession of China proper, he retained the Ming framework: lawsuits in the provinces ascended step by step from county and prefecture to the governor-general or governor, while capital cases were consolidated in the Three Judicial Offices.

sentences.zh: 然明制三法司，刑部受天下刑名，都察院糾察，大理寺駮正。

translations.literal: Yet under the Ming system of the Three Judicial Offices, the Ministry of Justice received criminal cases from all under Heaven, the Censorate investigated and censured, and the Court of Revision reviewed and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming arrangement, the Three Judicial Offices divided labor: the Ministry of Justice received criminal cases from across the empire, the Censorate conducted surveillance and impeachment, and the Court of Revision reviewed and corrected judgments.

sentences.zh: 清則外省刑案，統由刑部核覆。

translations.literal: Under the Qing, criminal cases from outer provinces were uniformly reviewed and confirmed by the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qing, criminal cases from the provinces were uniformly reviewed and ratified by the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 不會法者，院寺無由過問，應會法者，亦由刑部主稿。

translations.literal: Cases not requiring joint deliberation— the Court and Censorate had no means to intervene; cases requiring joint deliberation were also drafted chiefly by the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: For cases that did not require joint deliberation, the Court of Revision and Censorate had no avenue to intervene; even when joint deliberation was required, the Ministry of Justice still drafted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 在京訟獄，無論奏咨，俱由刑部審理，而部權特重。

translations.literal: Lawsuits and prisons in the capital, whether memorialized or reported, were all tried by the Ministry of Justice, and the ministry's authority was especially weighty.
translations.idiomatic: All litigation and detention in the capital, whether submitted by memorial or routine report, fell to the Ministry of Justice, whose authority was exceptionally heavy.

sentences.zh: 刑部初設十四司。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice was first set up with fourteen bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice was first organized into fourteen bureaus.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，添置現審左右二司，審理八旗命盜及各衙門欽發事件。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, the Left and Right Bureaus of Current Review were added to try cases of homicide and robbery among the Eight Banners and matters dispatched by imperial order from the various yamen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, Left and Right Bureaus of Current Review were added to handle Banner homicides and robberies and cases dispatched by imperial order from other agencies.

sentences.zh: 後復改並，定為十八清吏司：曰直隸，曰奉天，曰江蘇，曰安徽，曰江西，曰福建，曰浙江，曰湖廣，曰山東，曰山西，曰陝西，曰四川，曰廣東，曰廣西，曰雲南，曰貴州。

translations.literal: Later they were again reorganized and merged, fixed as eighteen Bureaus of Pure Officials: namely Zhili, Fengtian, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Huguang, Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They were later reorganized again into eighteen Bureaus of Pure Officials: Zhili, Fengtian, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Huguang, Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 凡各省刑名咨揭到部，各司具稿呈堂，以定準駮。

translations.literal: Whenever criminal reports and memorials from the provinces arrived at the ministry, each bureau prepared drafts and presented them to the hall to fix approval or rejection.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever provincial criminal reports reached the ministry, each bureau drafted a recommendation for the chief ministers, who then decided approval or rejection.

sentences.zh: 吉林、黑龍江附諸奉天，甘肅、新疆附諸陝西，京曹各署關涉文件，亦分隸於十七司。

translations.literal: Jilin and Heilongjiang were attached to Fengtian; Gansu and Xinjiang to Shaanxi; documents from the capital bureaus were also divided and subordinated among the seventeen bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin and Heilongjiang were handled under Fengtian; Gansu and Xinjiang under Shaanxi; and paperwork from capital agencies was likewise distributed among the seventeen bureaus.

sentences.zh: 現審則輪流簽分。

translations.literal: Current review cases were assigned by rotation through signing.
translations.idiomatic: Current-review cases were assigned in rotation by signature.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，設督捕衙門，置侍郎滿、漢各一員，其屬有前司、後司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi, the Office of Pursuit and Capture was established, with one Manchu and one Han vice minister each; its subordinates had a Front Bureau and a Rear Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Shunzhi, the Office of Pursuit and Capture was established with one Manchu and one Han vice minister, supported by Front and Rear Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 初隸兵部，專理緝捕逃旗事宜。

translations.literal: At first subordinate to the Ministry of War, it specialized in pursuing and capturing fugitive bannermen.
translations.idiomatic: It was initially subordinate to the Ministry of War and specialized in hunting down fugitive bannermen.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年裁撤，將前後司改隸刑部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi it was abolished, and the Front and Rear Bureaus were transferred to subordination under the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi it was abolished, and its Front and Rear Bureaus were transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 嗣復並為督捕一司，不掌外省刑名，亦不分現審。

translations.literal: Later they were again merged into one Bureau of Pursuit and Capture, which did not manage outer-province criminal cases and also did not share current review.
translations.idiomatic: They were later merged into a single Bureau of Pursuit and Capture, which neither handled provincial criminal cases nor took part in current-review rotation.

sentences.zh: 刑部收受訟案，已結未結，每月匯奏。

translations.literal: Cases received by the Ministry of Justice, whether concluded or not, were summarized and memorialized monthly.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice reported monthly on all cases received, concluded or pending.

sentences.zh: 設督催所，而督以例限。

translations.literal: A Supervision and Urging Office was established to supervise by statutory time limits.
translations.idiomatic: A Supervision and Urging Office was established to enforce the statutory deadlines.

sentences.zh: 審結尋常徒、流、軍、遣等罪，按季匯題。

translations.literal: Ordinary cases of penal servitude, exile, military exile, and banishment, once tried and concluded, were summarized by topic each quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Routine sentences of penal servitude, exile, military exile, and banishment, once concluded, were reported quarterly in summary memorials.

sentences.zh: 案系奏交，情雖輕，專案奏結。

translations.literal: Cases referred by imperial memorial, though the circumstances were light, were concluded by special memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Cases referred to the throne by memorial, however light the circumstances, required a separate concluding memorial.

sentences.zh: 死罪既取供，大理寺委寺丞或評事，都察院委御史，赴本司會審，謂之會小法。

translations.literal: Once capital crimes had obtained confession, the Court of Revision delegated a vice director or reviewer, the Censorate delegated a censor, and they went to the bureau for joint trial—called the minor joint review.
translations.idiomatic: After confessions were obtained in capital cases, the Court of Revision sent a vice director or reviewer and the Censorate a censor to join the responsible bureau for a preliminary joint review—the "minor joint review."

sentences.zh: 獄成呈堂，都察院左都御史或左副都御史，大理寺卿或少卿，挈同屬員赴刑部會審，謂之會大法。

translations.literal: When the case was complete and presented to the hall, the Censorate's left censor-in-chief or left vice censor-in-chief and the Court's chief or vice chief, leading their subordinates, went to the Ministry of Justice for joint trial—called the major joint review.
translations.idiomatic: When the file was complete and brought before the chief ministers, the left censor-in-chief or left vice censor-in-chief of the Censorate and the chief or vice chief of the Court of Revision, with their staffs, joined the Ministry of Justice for the "major joint review."

sentences.zh: 如有翻異，發司覆審，否則會稿分別題奏。

translations.literal: If there was reversal or discrepancy, the bureau was ordered to re-try; otherwise the joint draft was separately memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: If the parties changed their testimony, the case was sent back for retrial; otherwise the joint draft was memorialized in the usual form.

sentences.zh: 罪干立決，旨下，本司派員監刑。

translations.literal: Crimes touching immediate execution—once the edict descended, the bureau dispatched officers to supervise the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: For crimes warranting immediate execution, once the edict arrived the responsible bureau dispatched officers to supervise the sentence.

sentences.zh: 監候則入朝審。

translations.literal: Those held awaiting execution entered the court review.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners held awaiting execution were referred to the court review.

sentences.zh: 各省戶、婚、田土及笞、杖輕罪，由州縣完結，例稱自理。

translations.literal: In each province, household, marriage, land, and light crimes of beating with the rod or the stick were concluded by prefecture and county, customarily called self-adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, household, marriage, land, and minor beating offenses were concluded at the county or prefecture level—cases "adjudicated locally."

sentences.zh: 詞訟每月設立循環簿，申送督、撫、司、道查考。

translations.literal: Litigation each month established a rotating register, reported upward to governor-general, governor, provincial judge, and circuit intendant for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Each month a rotating litigation register was kept and forwarded to the governor-general, governor, provincial judge, and circuit intendant for review.

sentences.zh: 巡道巡歷所至，提簿查核，如有未完，勒限催審。

translations.literal: Wherever the touring circuit intendant traveled on inspection, he took up the register to check; if cases were unfinished, he set a deadline and urged trial.
translations.idiomatic: When a circuit intendant made his inspection rounds, he examined the register on the spot and, if cases remained open, imposed deadlines to hurry them to judgment.

sentences.zh: 徒以上解府、道、臬司審轉，徒罪由督撫匯案咨結。

translations.literal: Penal servitude and above were sent up to prefecture, circuit, and provincial judicial commissioner for review and transmission; penal-servitude cases were gathered by governor-general or governor and reported for conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Sentences of penal servitude and above were escalated through prefecture, circuit, and provincial judicial commissioner; penal-servitude cases were bundled by the governor or governor-general and reported for closure.

sentences.zh: 有關人命及流以上，專咨由部匯題。

translations.literal: Cases involving human life and exile and above were specially reported to the ministry and summarized by topic.
translations.idiomatic: Cases involving loss of life or exile and heavier punishments were reported separately to the ministry for inclusion in summary memorials.

sentences.zh: 死罪系謀反、大逆、惡逆、不道、劫獄、反獄、戕官，並洋盜、會匪、強盜、拒殺官差，罪干凌遲、斬、梟者，專摺具奏，交部速議。

translations.literal: Capital crimes involving treason, great sedition, wicked sedition, impiety, prison raid, prison revolt, killing officials, together with foreign pirates, secret-society bandits, robbers, and killing officials or runners while resisting— crimes touching dismemberment, decapitation, or display of the head— were specially memorialized by folded dispatch and handed to the ministry for rapid deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes of treason, great sedition, wicked sedition, impiety, prison raids or revolts, murder of officials, foreign piracy, secret-society banditry, robbery, or killing officials or runners while resisting—when the sentence was dismemberment, decapitation, or exposure of the head—were reported by special folded memorial for rapid ministry deliberation.

sentences.zh: 殺一家二命之案，交部速題。

translations.literal: Cases of killing two persons in one household were handed to the ministry for rapid memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Cases involving two deaths in a single household were sent to the ministry for expedited memorial.

sentences.zh: 其餘斬、絞，俱專本具題，分送揭帖於法司科道，內閣票擬，交三法司核議。

translations.literal: All other decapitation and strangulation cases were likewise memorialized by special report; summary slips were distributed to the judicial censors of the Three Offices, the Grand Secretariat drafted rescripts, and they were handed to the Three Judicial Offices for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: All other decapitation and strangulation cases were likewise submitted by special memorial; summary slips went to the judicial censors, the Grand Secretariat drafted rescripts, and the Three Judicial Offices conducted joint review.

sentences.zh: 如情罪不符及引律錯誤者，或駮令覆審，或徑行改正，合則如擬核定。

translations.literal: If circumstances and crime did not match or statutes were wrongly cited, either rejection ordered re-trial, or correction was made directly; if fitting, approval followed the proposed sentence.
translations.idiomatic: If the facts did not match the charge or the statutes were misapplied, the case might be sent back for retrial or corrected outright; if correct, the proposed sentence was ratified.

sentences.zh: 議上立決，命下，釘封飛遞各州縣正印官或佐貳，會同武職行刑。

translations.literal: When deliberation approved immediate execution and the command descended, sealed dispatches were rushed to each prefecture and county's seal-holding official or deputy, who together with military officers carried out the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Once immediate execution was approved and the order issued, sealed dispatches were rushed to the chief civil officer or deputy at each prefecture and county, who carried out the sentence jointly with the local military officer.

sentences.zh: 監候則入秋審。

translations.literal: Those held awaiting execution entered the autumn review.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners held awaiting execution entered the autumn review.

sentences.zh: 朝審原於明天順三年，令每歲霜降後，但有該決重囚，三法司會同公、侯、伯從實審錄。

translations.literal: Court review originated in the third year of Tianshun of Ming, ordering that after the Frost's Descent each year, whenever there were heavy prisoners due for execution, the Three Judicial Offices together with dukes, marquises, and earls should examine and record according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: Court review originated in Ming Tianshun 3, when it was ordered that after the Frost's Descent each year the Three Judicial Offices, together with dukes, marquises, and earls, should examine all capital prisoners due for execution and record their findings according to the facts.

sentences.zh: 秋審亦原於明之奏決單，冬至前會審決之。

translations.literal: Autumn review also originated in the Ming memorial-decision slip, with joint review and decision before the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn review likewise derived from the Ming "memorial decision" procedure, with joint review and final disposition completed before the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，刑部左侍郎黨崇雅奏言：「舊制凡刑獄重犯，自大逆、大盜決不待時外，餘俱監候處決。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, the Ministry of Justice's left vice minister Dang Chongya memorialized: "Under the old system, for all heavy criminals in prisons, except great sedition and great robbery, which were executed without delay, the rest were all held awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1, Dang Chongya, left vice minister of the Ministry of Justice, memorialized: "Under the former system, all serious prisoners except those guilty of great sedition or great robbery—who were executed at once—were held in custody awaiting sentence.

sentences.zh: 在京有熱審、朝審之例，每至霜降後方請旨處決。

translations.literal: In the capital there were the precedents of summer review and court review; only after Frost's Descent each year was imperial instruction sought for execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the summer review and court review applied, and execution required imperial approval only after the Frost's Descent.

sentences.zh: 在外直省，亦有三司秋審之例，未嘗一麗死刑輒棄於市。

translations.literal: In the outer provinces directly administered, there was also the precedent of the three offices' autumn review; never was a death sentence immediately cast upon the market.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces as well, the three offices conducted autumn review, and a death sentence was never carried out the moment it was pronounced.

sentences.zh: 望照例區別，以昭欽恤。」

translations.literal: It is hoped that distinction will be made according to precedent, to display imperial compassion.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the old distinctions be preserved, to manifest the throne's compassionate regard for human life."

sentences.zh: 此有清言秋、朝審之始。

translations.literal: This is where Qing statements on the beginning of autumn and court review start.
translations.idiomatic: This passage marks the Qing dynasty's own account of how autumn and court review began.

sentences.zh: 嗣後逐漸舉行，而法益加密。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was gradually implemented, and the law grew ever more stringent.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was gradually extended thereafter, and the procedures grew ever more elaborate.

sentences.zh: 初制分情實、緩決、矜、疑，然疑獄不經見。

translations.literal: The initial system divided deserving execution, deferred decision, compassion, and doubt; yet doubtful cases were rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: The original categories were deserving execution, deferred decision, meriting compassion, and doubtful—but doubtful cases were seldom encountered.

sentences.zh: 雍正以後，加入留養承祀，區為五類。

translations.literal: After Yongzheng, retention for family support and sacrificial rites was added, dividing into five categories.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongzheng reign, retention for family support and sacrificial duties was added, making five categories in all.

sentences.zh: 截止日期，雲南、貴州、四川、廣東、廣西以年前封印日，福建以正月三十日，奉天、吉林、黑龍江、陝西、甘肅、湖北、湖南、浙江、江西、安徽、江蘇以月初十日，河南、山東、山西以三月初十日，直隸以三月三十日。

translations.literal: Cutoff dates: Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Guangdong, and Guangxi by the year's end seal day; Fujian by the thirtieth day of the first month; Fengtian, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Anhui, and Jiangsu by the tenth day of the first month; Henan, Shandong, and Shanxi by the tenth day of the third month; Zhili by the thirtieth day of the third month.
translations.idiomatic: Cutoff dates varied by province: Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Guangdong, and Guangxi used the year-end seal date; Fujian, the thirtieth day of the first month; Fengtian, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Anhui, and Jiangsu, the tenth day of the first month; Henan, Shandong, and Shanxi, the tenth day of the third month; and Zhili, the thirtieth day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 然遇情重之案，雖後期有聲明趕入秋審者。

translations.literal: Yet when encountering cases of grave circumstances, even after the deadline there were declarations to rush them into autumn review.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, especially grave cases could still be declared for rushed inclusion in the autumn review after the regular deadline.

sentences.zh: 刑部各司，自歲首將各省截止期前題准之案，分類編冊，發交司員看詳。

translations.literal: From the year's start each bureau of the Ministry of Justice classified into registers cases approved by memorial from the provinces before the cutoff, and distributed them to bureau officers for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of each year the ministry's bureaus compiled registers of cases approved from the provinces before the cutoff and assigned them to clerks for detailed review.

sentences.zh: 初看藍筆句改，覆看用紫，輪遞至秋審處坐辦、律例館提調，墨書粘簽，一一詳加斟酌，而後呈堂核閱。

translations.literal: First review used blue ink for sentence revision; second review used purple; rotation passed to the autumn-review resident officer and the Code and Statutes Office chief compiler, who wrote in black ink and pasted labels, deliberating each in detail, and then presented to the hall for verification.
translations.idiomatic: The first reader marked revisions in blue, the second in purple; cases then rotated to the autumn-review resident officer and the Code and Statutes Office compiler, who annotated in black, attached labels, and weighed each point before the chiefs reviewed the file.

sentences.zh: 朝審本刑部問擬之案，刑部自定實緩。

translations.literal: Court review cases were originally those proposed by the Ministry of Justice after inquiry; the ministry itself fixed deserving execution or deferral.
translations.idiomatic: Court review covered cases the Ministry of Justice had already proposed after inquiry, and the ministry itself classified them as deserving execution or deferred.

sentences.zh: 秋審則直省各督撫於應勘時，將人犯提解省城，率同在省司道公同會勘，定擬具題。

translations.literal: For autumn review, each governor-general and governor of the directly administered provinces, at the time for investigation, escorted the prisoners to the provincial capital, led the provincial judicial and circuit officials in joint investigation, fixed the proposal, and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: For autumn review each governor or governor-general, when investigation was due, had the prisoners brought to the provincial capital, convened the provincial judicial and circuit officials for joint review, and memorialized with a proposed classification.

sentences.zh: 刑部俟定限五月中旬以前，各省後尾到齊，查閱外勘與部擬不符者，別列一冊。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice waited until the fixed limit before mid-fifth month, when the last arrivals from the provinces were all in, and examined cases where outer investigation and ministry proposal did not match, listing them separately in another register.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry waited until mid-fifth month, when the last provincial reports had arrived, then singled out cases in which the provincial finding disagreed with the ministry's proposal into a separate register.

sentences.zh: 始則司議，提調、坐辦主之。

translations.literal: At first there was bureau deliberation, led by the chief compiler and resident officer.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation began at bureau level under the compiler and resident officer.

sentences.zh: 繼則堂議，六堂主之，司議各員與焉。

translations.literal: Next came hall deliberation, presided over by the six chiefs, with all bureau deliberators participating.
translations.idiomatic: It then moved to deliberation by the six chief ministers, with the bureau officers participating.

sentences.zh: 議定，刑部將原案及法司督撫各勘語刊刷招冊，送九卿、詹事、科道各一分，八月內定期在金水橋西會同詳核。

translations.literal: Once deliberation was settled, the Ministry of Justice printed casebooks of the original cases and the investigation statements of the judicial offices, governors, and governors-general, sending one copy each to the Nine Ministers, Household Officials of the Heir Apparent, and Censors; within the eighth month a fixed date was set for joint detailed verification west of the Jinshui Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When deliberation was complete, the ministry printed casebooks containing the original files and the findings of the judicial offices and provincial authorities, distributed one copy each to the Nine Ministers, Household Officials of the Heir Apparent, and censors, and scheduled a joint review west of the Jinshui Bridge during the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 先日朝審，三法司、九卿、詹事、科道入座，刑部將監內應死人犯提至當堂，命吏朗誦罪狀及定擬實、緩節略，事畢回禁。

translations.literal: On the prior day was court review: the Three Judicial Offices, Nine Ministers, Household Officials, and Censors took their seats; the Ministry of Justice brought the prisoners in the prison due for death to the hall, ordered clerks to read aloud the crimes and the summarized classification of deserving execution or deferral, and when finished returned them to detention.
translations.idiomatic: Court review came first: the Three Judicial Offices, Nine Ministers, Household Officials, and censors took their seats while the ministry brought capital prisoners before the hall, had clerks read aloud the charges and proposed classifications, and returned them to detention when finished.

sentences.zh: 次日秋審，憑招冊審核，如俱無異議，會同將原擬陸續具題；

translations.literal: The next day was autumn review, verifying against the casebooks; if all were without objection, they jointly memorialized the original proposals in succession;
translations.idiomatic: Autumn review followed the next day. If the casebooks aroused no objection, the participants jointly memorialized the original proposals in turn;

sentences.zh: 有異，前期簽商。

translations.literal: if there was objection, they signed and consulted beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: where there was disagreement, they negotiated by signed memoranda beforehand.

sentences.zh: 若各執不相下，持異之人奏上，類由刑部回奏聽裁。

translations.literal: If each side held firm and would not yield, the person holding the dissent memorialized upward; generally the Ministry of Justice memorialized in reply for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: If neither side would yield, the dissenting party memorialized the throne, and the Ministry of Justice usually replied with a memorial for the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 苟攻及原審，則徑行扣除再訊。

translations.literal: If the attack reached the original trial, the case was directly struck out for re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: If the challenge struck at the original trial, the case was struck from the list and sent back for reinvestigation.

sentences.zh: 二百餘年來，刑部歷辦秋、朝審，句稽講貫，備極周密，長官每以此校司員之優劣。

translations.literal: For more than two hundred years the Ministry of Justice has handled autumn and court review, examining and explaining with exhaustive thoroughness; superiors often used this to gauge the superiority or inferiority of bureau officers.
translations.idiomatic: For more than two centuries the Ministry of Justice has conducted autumn and court review with painstaking thoroughness, and chiefs routinely used a clerk's performance on these cases to judge his ability.

sentences.zh: 究之人命至重，死者不可復生，其所矜慎，尤在實、緩。

translations.literal: After all, human life is supremely weighty; the dead cannot be revived; what they especially treat with compassion and caution lies in deserving execution and deferral.
translations.idiomatic: Human life is paramount—the dead cannot be restored—and the greatest caution was exercised precisely over the categories of deserving execution and deferred decision.

sentences.zh: 乾隆以前，各司隨意定擬，每不畫一。

translations.literal: Before Qianlong, each bureau fixed proposals at will, often not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Qianlong reign each bureau classified cases as it saw fit, with little consistency.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，始酌定比對條款四十則，刊分各司，並頒諸各省，以為勘擬之準繩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, forty articles of comparative clauses were first weighed and fixed, printed and distributed to each bureau, and also promulgated to all provinces as the standard for investigation and proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In his thirty-second year the emperor promulgated forty comparative guidelines, distributed them to each bureau and to every province, and made them the standard for classification.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，復行增輯。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, they were again expanded and edited.
translations.idiomatic: In his forty-ninth year the guidelines were expanded and revised again.

sentences.zh: 嗣刑部侍郎阮葵生別輯秋讞志略，而後規矩略備，中外言秋勘者依之，並比附歷年成案，故秋、朝審會議，其持異特奏者，每不勝焉。

translations.literal: Later Vice Minister of Justice Ruan Kuisheng separately compiled the Brief Record of Autumn Verdicts, and thereafter rules were roughly complete; inside and outside, those who spoke of autumn investigation followed it, also comparing and attaching yearly precedents; therefore at autumn and court review conferences, those who held dissent and specially memorialized were often unable to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Later Vice Minister Ruan Kuisheng compiled the Brief Record of Autumn Verdicts, bringing the rules to rough completeness. Officials throughout the empire who handled autumn review relied on it and cited precedents from past years, so dissenters at the autumn and court review conferences seldom carried the day.

sentences.zh: 秋審本上，入緩決者，得旨後，刑部將戲殺、誤殺、擅殺之犯，奏減杖一百，流三千里，竊贓滿貫、三犯竊贓至五十兩以上之犯，奏減雲、貴、兩廣極邊、煙瘴充軍，其餘仍舊監固，俟秋審三次後查辦。

translations.literal: When the autumn-review memorial was approved, those entering deferred decision—after receiving the edict—the Ministry of Justice memorialized reduction for offenders of playful killing, mistaken killing, and unauthorized killing to one hundred blows of the stick and exile three thousand li; for theft reaching the full quota and three-time theft reaching fifty taels or more, memorialized reduction to military exile in the extreme border and miasma regions of Yunnan, Guizhou, and the two Guangs; the rest remained in prison as before, awaiting handling after three autumn reviews.
translations.idiomatic: After the autumn-review memorial was approved, prisoners classified as deferred might receive further reductions: the ministry memorialized that playful, mistaken, or unauthorized killers be reduced to one hundred blows and exile three thousand li; habitual thieves reaching fifty taels or more, to military exile in the miasma frontiers of Yunnan, Guizhou, and the two Guangs; all others remained in custody until reviewed after three autumn sessions.

sentences.zh: 間有初次入緩，後復改實者，權操自上，非常例也。

translations.literal: Occasionally there were those who first entered deferral but later were changed to deserving execution; authority rested with the throne above, not a regular precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally a prisoner first classified as deferred was later reclassified as deserving execution—a prerogative exercised by the throne itself, not a routine procedure.

sentences.zh: 入可矜者，或減流，或減徒。

translations.literal: Those entering meriting compassion were either reduced from exile or reduced from penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Those classified as meriting compassion might have exile or penal servitude reduced.

sentences.zh: 留養承祀者，將該犯枷號兩月，責四十板釋放。

translations.literal: Those retained for family support and sacrificial rites were cangued for two months, ordered forty blows of the board, and released.
translations.idiomatic: Those retained to support parents and maintain ancestral sacrifices were cangued for two months, given forty blows of the paddle, and released.

sentences.zh: 案系斗殺，追銀二十兩給死者家屬養贍。

translations.literal: If the case was brawl killing, twenty taels of silver were pursued and given to the victim's family for support.
translations.idiomatic: In brawl-killing cases twenty taels of silver were levied for the victim's family's support.

sentences.zh: 情實則大別有三，服制、官犯、常犯是也。

translations.literal: Deserving execution was broadly divided into three: mourning-regulation cases, official offenders, and ordinary offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Deserving execution fell into three broad types: mourning-regulation cases, official offenders, and ordinary offenders.

sentences.zh: 本下，內閣隨命欽天監分期擇日。

translations.literal: Once the memorial descended, the Grand Secretariat at once ordered the Directorate of Astronomy to choose dates by stages.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial was approved, the Grand Secretariat ordered the Directorate of Astronomy to set execution dates in stages.

sentences.zh: 句到，刑部按期進呈黃冊。

translations.literal: When the execution date arrived, the Ministry of Justice presented the yellow register on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: On each execution day the ministry presented the yellow register on schedule.

sentences.zh: 至日，素服御殿，大學士三法司侍，上秉硃筆，或命大學士按單予句。

translations.literal: On the day, in plain dress he held court in the hall; Grand Secretaries and the Three Judicial Offices attended; the emperor took the vermilion brush, or ordered Grand Secretaries to grant execution according to the list.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor appeared in plain dress, attended by Grand Secretaries and the Three Judicial Offices, took up the vermilion brush, or delegated to the Grand Secretaries to mark executions on the list.

sentences.zh: 服制冊大都殺傷期功尊長之案，既以情輕而改監候，類不句決；

translations.literal: The mourning-regulation register mostly contained cases of killing or wounding agnates within one degree beyond the mourning circle; having been changed to held awaiting execution because circumstances were light, they generally were not granted execution;
translations.idiomatic: The mourning-regulation register mostly covered cases of killing or wounding senior relatives within the mourning circle; because the original sentence had been commuted to imprisonment awaiting review, execution was usually withheld;

sentences.zh: 情實二次，大學士會同刑部奏請改緩。

translations.literal: after two times classified as deserving execution, Grand Secretaries together with the Ministry of Justice memorialized requesting change to deferral.
translations.idiomatic: after two classifications as deserving execution, the Grand Secretaries and Ministry of Justice jointly memorialized to change the sentence to deferred.

sentences.zh: 官犯則情重者，刑部從嚴聲敘，未容倖免；

translations.literal: For official offenders, when circumstances were heavy the Ministry of Justice narrated strictly from severity, not permitting escape;
translations.idiomatic: For official offenders in grave cases the ministry argued strictly for execution, allowing no reprieve;

sentences.zh: 輕則一律免句，十次改緩。

translations.literal: when light, all alike were exempted from execution; after ten times changed to deferral.
translations.idiomatic: lighter cases were uniformly spared execution, and after ten appearances reclassified as deferred.

sentences.zh: 常犯之入情實，固罪無可逭者；

translations.literal: Ordinary offenders entering deserving execution—indeed the crime could not be escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary offenders classified as deserving execution had, in principle, no escape from the penalty;

sentences.zh: 其或一線可原，刑部粘簽聲敘，類多邀恩不句，十次亦改緩。

translations.literal: yet if there was a thread that could be excused, the Ministry of Justice pasted a label and narrated, mostly inviting grace without execution; after ten times also changed to deferral.
translations.idiomatic: yet if even a slender thread of excuse remained, the ministry attached a label pleading for mercy, and execution was usually withheld; after ten appearances the sentence might be changed to deferred as well.

sentences.zh: 向例句決重囚，刑科三覆奏，自乾隆十四年簡去二覆，第於句到前五日，覆奏一次。

translations.literal: Formerly, granting execution for heavy prisoners required three re-memorials from the Ministry of Justice censorate; from the fourteenth year of Qianlong two re-memorials were simplified away, leaving only one re-memorial five days before the execution date.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, execution of capital prisoners required three re-memorials from the Ministry of Justice censorate; from Qianlong 14 two of these were dropped, leaving a single re-memorial five days before the execution date.

sentences.zh: 句到時，將原本進呈覆閱，一俟批發，在京例由刑科給事中、刑部侍郎各一人赴西市監視。

translations.literal: When the execution date arrived, the original document was presented for re-reading; once the rescript was issued, in the capital the usual practice was for one supervising secretary of the Ministry of Justice censorate and one vice minister of the Ministry of Justice to go to the West Market to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: On the execution day the original memorial was presented again for the emperor's review; once the rescript issued, one supervising secretary from the Ministry of Justice censorate and one vice minister customarily supervised at the West Market.

sentences.zh: 官犯無論句否，俱綁赴行刑場候決。

translations.literal: Official offenders, whether granted execution or not, were all bound and taken to the execution ground to await decision.
translations.idiomatic: Official offenders, whether marked for execution or not, were bound and taken to the execution ground to await the final decision.

sentences.zh: 在外則刑部各司將句單連同榜示釘封送兵部發驛，文到之日行刑。

translations.literal: Outside the capital, each bureau of the Ministry of Justice sealed the execution list together with the public notice and sent it through the Ministry of War by courier relay; on the day the document arrived, execution was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces each bureau sealed the execution list with the public notice and sent it through the Ministry of War by courier; the sentence was carried out on the day the dispatch arrived.

sentences.zh: 如恭逢慶典或國家有故，則下旨停句。

translations.literal: If there happened to be a celebration or the state had occasion, an edict was issued to suspend execution.
translations.idiomatic: If a celebration occurred or the state faced extraordinary circumstances, an edict suspended executions.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，諭刑部：「朝審秋決，系刑獄重典。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, an instruction was issued to the Ministry of Justice: "Court review and autumn execution are great statutes of the prisons.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 the throne instructed the Ministry of Justice: "Court review and autumn execution are grave matters of criminal justice.

sentences.zh: 朕必詳閱招案始末，情形允協，令死者無冤。

translations.literal: I must read in detail the beginning and end of each casebook, that the circumstances accord, and let the dead be without injustice.
translations.idiomatic: I must read each casebook through from start to finish, ensure the facts fit the charge, and see that the condemned die without injustice.

sentences.zh: 今烸期伊邇，朝審甫竣，招冊繁多，尚未及詳細簡閱，驟行正法，朕心不忍。

translations.literal: Now the execution date draws near; court review has just ended, the casebooks are numerous, and I have not yet had time to review them in detail; to carry out execution at once—my heart cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The execution season is upon us, court review has only just ended, and the casebooks are too many for me to have reviewed them all in detail. To put them to death at once—I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 今年姑著暫停秋決，昭朕矜恤至意。」

translations.literal: This year let autumn execution be temporarily suspended, to display my utmost compassionate regard.
translations.idiomatic: Suspend autumn executions for this year, to show my utmost regard for human life."

sentences.zh: 自是列朝於秋讞俱勤慎校閱。

translations.literal: From this time onward, successive reigns all reviewed autumn verdicts with diligence and care.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every reign handled autumn verdicts with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十二年，聖袓御懋勤殿，召大學士、學士等入，酌定在京秋審情實重犯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi, the Sage Ancestor held court in the Hall of Diligent Government, summoned Grand Secretaries, academicians, and others to enter, and weighed the capital autumn-review cases deserving execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 the Sage Ancestor held court in the Hall of Diligent Government, summoned Grand Secretaries and academicians, and classified capital prisoners for autumn review.

sentences.zh: 聖袓取罪案逐一親閱，再三詳審，其斷無可恕者，始定情實。

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor took each crime case and personally read it one by one, examining again and again in detail; only those absolutely without forgiveness were fixed as deserving execution.
translations.idiomatic: He read every case himself, examining each again and again; only those beyond all excuse were marked deserving execution.

sentences.zh: 因諭曰：「人命事關重大，故召爾等共相商酌。

translations.literal: He thereupon instructed: "Human life concerns weighty matters; therefore I have summoned you to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Human life is a grave matter, which is why I have called you to deliberate together.

sentences.zh: 情有可原，即開生路。」

translations.literal: If circumstances permit excuse, open a path to life at once.
translations.idiomatic: Where circumstances permit mercy, open a path to life."

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，世宗御洞明堂，閱秋審情實招冊，諭刑部曰：「諸臣所進招冊，俱經細加斟酌，擬定情實。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, the Shizong held court in the Bright Hall of Enlightenment, reviewed the autumn-review casebooks of those deserving execution, and instructed the Ministry of Justice: "The casebooks submitted by the various officials have all been finely weighed and deliberated, fixing deserving execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 11 the Shizong held court in the Bright Hall of Enlightenment, reviewed autumn-review casebooks, and told the Ministry of Justice: "The casebooks your officials have submitted have all been carefully weighed and classified as deserving execution.

sentences.zh: 但此內有一線可生之機，爾等亦當陳奏。

translations.literal: Yet if within them there is a thread of possibility for life, you also ought to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: But if even a thread of life remains possible, you must say so in memorial.

sentences.zh: 在前日定擬情實，自是執法，在此刻句到商酌，又當原情，斷不可因前奏難更，遂爾隱默也。」

translations.literal: To fix deserving execution on a prior day was of course enforcing the law; at this moment, when execution is at hand and deliberation is held, one must also consider the circumstances—by no means may you remain silent because a prior memorial is hard to change.
translations.idiomatic: Fixing deserving execution earlier was enforcing the law; at the moment of execution you must weigh the human circumstances again—you must not stay silent because an earlier memorial is hard to change."

sentences.zh: 高宗尤垂意刑名，秋審冊上，每干飭責。

translations.literal: The Gaozong especially attended to criminal matters; on autumn-review registers he often issued reprimands.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong paid special attention to criminal matters and often reprimanded officials on the autumn-review registers.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年，湖南官犯饒佺，以其回護己過予句。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong, the Hunan official offender Rao Qian was granted execution for shielding his own fault.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 31 the Hunan official offender Rao Qian was marked for execution for shielding his own misconduct.

sentences.zh: 迨閱浙省招冊，知府高象震亦以承審回護，原題僅擬軍台效力。

translations.literal: When he came to review the Zhejiang casebook, Prefect Gao Xiangzhen likewise shielded himself in trial, yet the original memorial had only proposed service at a military post.
translations.idiomatic: When he reviewed the Zhejiang casebook, he found Prefect Gao Xiangzhen had likewise shielded himself during trial, though the original memorial had proposed only service at a military post.

sentences.zh: 急諭湖南巡撫將饒佺暫停處決，令刑部查明兩案情節不同，始行明諭處分。

translations.literal: He urgently instructed the Hunan governor to suspend Rao Qian's execution, ordered the Ministry of Justice to ascertain that the circumstances of the two cases differed, and only then issued clear instructions on disposition.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently ordered the Hunan governor to suspend Rao Qian's execution, told the ministry to establish that the two cases differed in circumstance, and only then issued clear instructions on punishment.

sentences.zh: 其慎重讞典如此。

translations.literal: Such was the care taken with verdict statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the care the throne took with capital verdicts.

sentences.zh: 仁宗亦嫻習法律。

translations.literal: The Renzong was also well versed in law.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong was likewise well versed in law.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年，御史廣興會議秋審，奏請將斗殺擬緩之廣東姚得輝改入情實，援引乾隆十八年「一命必有一抵」之旨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing, Censor Guangxing at the autumn-review conference memorialized requesting that Yao Dehui of Guangdong, proposed for deferral in a brawl killing, be changed to deserving execution, citing the Qianlong eighteenth-year instruction that "one life must have one compensation."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 7, at the autumn-review conference, Censor Guangxing asked that Yao Dehui of Guangdong—a brawl killer proposed for deferral—be reclassified as deserving execution, citing the Qianlong 18 instruction that "one life must have one compensation."

sentences.zh: 仁宗謂：「一命一抵，原指械鬥等案而言，至尋常鬥毆，各斃各命，自當酌情理之平，分別實緩。

translations.literal: The Renzong said: "One life for one compensation originally referred to cases of armed brawls and the like; as for ordinary brawls, each side kills and each dies—one should weigh the balance of reason and feeling and distinguish deserving execution from deferral.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong replied: "One life for one compensation referred to armed brawls and the like. In ordinary brawls each side kills and dies; reason and feeling must be weighed to distinguish deserving execution from deferral.

sentences.zh: 若拘泥『一命必有一抵』之語，則是秋讞囚徒，凡殺傷斃命之案，將盡行問擬情實，可不必有緩決一項。

translations.literal: If one rigidly clings to the phrase 'one life must have one compensation,' then among autumn-review prisoners, for all cases of killing or wounding with death, all would be proposed as deserving execution, and there would be no need for the category of deferred decision.
translations.idiomatic: If we rigidly applied 'one life must have one compensation' to every killing, every autumn-review prisoner would be marked deserving execution and the category of deferred decision would become pointless."

sentences.zh: 有是理乎？」

translations.literal: Is there such a principle?
translations.idiomatic: Would that make any sense?"

sentences.zh: 命仍照原擬入緩。

translations.literal: He ordered that the original proposal of deferral still be followed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the original classification of deferral to stand."

sentences.zh: 其剖析法意，致為明允。

translations.literal: His parsing of legal meaning reached exceptional clarity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: His parsing of the law was exceptionally clear and fair.

sentences.zh: 自後宣宗、文宗遵循前軌，罕可紀述。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Xuanzong and Wenzong followed the former track, with little worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong and Wenzong followed precedent, with little worth recording.

sentences.zh: 穆宗、德宗兩經垂簾，每逢句到，命大學士一人捧單入內閣恭代，後遂沿為故事。

translations.literal: Under the Muzong and Dezong, during two regencies, whenever execution dates arrived, one Grand Secretary was ordered to carry the list into the Grand Secretariat to perform the ceremony by proxy; later this became a standing practice.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Muzong and Dezong, during two regencies, whenever execution dates arrived one Grand Secretary carried the list into the Grand Secretariat to act for the throne; this later became fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 而前行之秋審條款，因光緒季年死刑遞有減降，法律館重加釐定，奏頒內外焉。

translations.literal: The former autumn-review articles, because in the late Guangxu years capital punishment was progressively reduced, were revised and fixed anew by the Law Codification Office and memorialized for promulgation inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier autumn-review regulations were revised and promulgated by the Law Codification Office after capital punishments were progressively reduced in late Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 熱審之制，順治初賡續舉行。

translations.literal: The summer-review system was continued and implemented from early Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The summer-review system was continued from early Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，定每年小滿後十日起，至立秋前一日止，非實犯死罪及軍、流，俱量予減等。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi it was fixed that from ten days after Lesser Fullness each year until the day before the Beginning of Autumn, for all except true capital crimes and military exile or banishment, reductions by degree were granted as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 it was fixed that from ten days after Lesser Fullness until the day before Beginning of Autumn, all except true capital crimes and military exile or banishment might receive appropriate reduction.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，諭刑部停止。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, the Ministry of Justice was instructed to stop.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year the ministry was ordered to stop.

sentences.zh: 雍正初復行。

translations.literal: In early Yongzheng it was revived.
translations.idiomatic: It was revived in early Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆以後，第准免笞、杖，則遞行八折決放，枷號漸釋，餘不之及。

translations.literal: After Qianlong, only exemption from rod and stick was allowed; then eight-tenths sentencing and release were applied in succession, cangue gradually released, the rest not touched.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianlong only rod and stick punishments were exempted, applied at eight-tenths of the statutory penalty with gradual release from the cangue; other punishments were unaffected.

sentences.zh: 且惟京師行之，外省笞、杖自理，無從考核，具文而已，列朝無寒審，而有軍、流、遣犯隆冬停遣之例。

translations.literal: Moreover it was practiced only in the capital; in outer provinces rod and stick were self-adjudicated, without means of inspection—mere form on paper. No dynasty had winter review, but there was the precedent of suspending dispatch of military exiles, banished persons, and deportees in deep winter.
translations.idiomatic: It applied only in the capital; in the provinces rod and stick cases were locally adjudicated without oversight—empty form. No dynasty had winter review, but military exiles, banished persons, and deportees were not dispatched in deep winter.

sentences.zh: 未起解者，十月至正月終及六月俱停遣。

translations.literal: Those not yet escorted were not dispatched from the tenth month through the end of the first month, nor in the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners not yet dispatched were not sent from the tenth month through the first month, nor in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 若已至中途，至十一月初一日准停。

translations.literal: If already on the road, suspension was permitted from the first day of the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Those already en route might be halted from the first day of the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 倘抵配不遠，並發往東南省分，人犯有情原前進者，一體起解。

translations.literal: If the place of assignment was not far, or if sent to southeastern provinces, and the prisoner had circumstances warranting advance, all alike were escorted.
translations.idiomatic: If the destination was near, or if prisoners were bound for southeastern provinces and circumstances favored proceeding, they were dispatched as usual.

sentences.zh: 又有停審之例，每年正月、六月、十月及元旦令節七日，上元令節三日，端午、中秋、重陽各一日，萬壽聖節七日，各壇廟祭享、齋戒以及忌辰素服等日，並封印日期，四月初八日，每月初一、初二日、皆不理刑名。

translations.literal: There was also the precedent of suspending trials: each year the first, sixth, and tenth months and the seven days of New Year's festival, three days of the Lantern festival, one day each for Dragon Boat, Mid-Autumn, and Double Ninth festivals, seven days of the imperial birthday, days of sacrifice and fasting at the various altars and temples, mourning anniversaries in plain dress, and seal days, the eighth day of the fourth month, and the first and second days of each month—on all these criminal matters were not handled.
translations.idiomatic: Trials were also suspended on the first, sixth, and tenth months; the seven New Year festival days; three Lantern festival days; Dragon Boat, Mid-Autumn, and Double Ninth; seven imperial birthday days; altar sacrifices and fasts; mourning anniversaries in plain dress; seal days; the eighth day of the fourth month; and the first and second of each month.

sentences.zh: 然中外問刑衙門，於正月、六月、十月及封印日期、每月初一二等日不盡如例行也。

translations.literal: Yet criminal yamen inside and outside the capital on the first, sixth, and tenth months and seal days and the first and second of each month did not entirely follow the routine.
translations.idiomatic: Yet criminal offices throughout the empire did not always observe these days in full.

sentences.zh: 其農忙停審，則自四月初一日至七月三十日，一應戶、婚、田土細故，不準受理，刑事不在此限。

translations.literal: As for suspension during agricultural busy seasons, from the first day of the fourth month through the thirtieth day of the seventh month, all household, marriage, and land petty matters were not accepted; criminal cases were not within this limit.
translations.idiomatic: During the agricultural busy season, from the first day of the fourth month through the thirtieth of the seventh, household, marriage, and land disputes were not accepted; criminal cases were excepted.

sentences.zh: 又有停刑之例，每年正月、六月及冬至以前十日，夏至以前五日，一應立決人犯及秋、朝審處決重囚，皆停止行刑。

translations.literal: There was also the precedent of suspending punishment: each year the first and sixth months and the ten days before the winter solstice and five days before the summer solstice—all prisoners for immediate execution and heavy prisoners for autumn or court review—execution was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Executions were also suspended in the first and sixth months and the ten days before the winter solstice and five days before the summer solstice—for immediate executions and autumn or court review prisoners alike.

sentences.zh: 凡審級，直省以州縣正印官為初審。

translations.literal: As for trial levels, in directly administered provinces the seal-holding official of prefecture and county was the first trial.
translations.idiomatic: Trial levels in the provinces began with the seal-holding county or prefecture official as first instance.

sentences.zh: 不服，控府、控道、控司、控院，越訴者笞。

translations.literal: If not accepted, appeal to prefecture, circuit, provincial judge, or governor's office; those who skipped levels were beaten with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Appeals went to prefecture, circuit, provincial judge, or governor's office; skipping levels brought beating with the rod.

sentences.zh: 其有冤抑赴都察院、通政司或步軍統領衙門呈訴者，名曰京控。

translations.literal: Those with suppressed injustice who went to the Censorate, Office of Transmission, or the Metropolitan Infantry Command to lodge complaints were called capital appeals.
translations.idiomatic: Those who brought suppressed grievances to the Censorate, Office of Transmission, or Metropolitan Infantry Command were called capital appeals.

sentences.zh: 登聞鼓，順治初立諸都察院。

translations.literal: The Petition Drum—in early Shunzhi it was established at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Petition Drum was first established at the Censorate in early Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改設右長安門外。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year it was moved outside the Right Chang'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year it was moved outside the Right Chang'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 每日科道官一員輪值。

translations.literal: Each day one censor on rotation was on duty.
translations.idiomatic: One censor served on rotation each day.

sentences.zh: 後移入通政司，別置鼓廳。

translations.literal: Later it was moved into the Office of Transmission and a separate drum hall was set up.
translations.idiomatic: It was later moved into the Office of Transmission with a separate drum hall.

sentences.zh: 其投廳擊鼓，或遇乘輿出郊，迎駕申訴者，名曰叩閽。

translations.literal: Those who entered the hall to strike the drum, or who met the imperial procession leaving the suburbs to present grievances, were called knocking at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Striking the drum in the hall, or presenting grievances when the imperial procession left the suburbs, was called knocking at the gate.

sentences.zh: 從前有擅入午門、長安門、堂子跪告，及打長安門內、正陽門外石獅鳴冤者，嚴禁始絕。

translations.literal: Formerly there were those who rashly entered the Meridian Gate, Chang'an Gate, or the Hall kneeling to complain, or who struck the stone lions inside Chang'an Gate or outside the Front Gate to voice injustice—all strictly forbidden and finally ended.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier practices—rushing the Meridian Gate, Chang'an Gate, or the Hall to kneel and complain, or striking the stone lions at Chang'an Gate or the Front Gate—were strictly forbidden and finally suppressed.

sentences.zh: 即迎車駕而衝突儀仗，亦罪至充軍。

translations.literal: Even meeting the imperial carriage and charging the guard of honor was punished up to military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Even charging the imperial guard of honor when meeting the carriage was punished with military exile.

sentences.zh: 京控及叩閽之案，或發回該省督撫，或奏交刑部提訊。

translations.literal: Capital-appeal and gate-knocking cases were either sent back to the provincial governor-general or governor, or memorialized to the Ministry of Justice for escorted interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital appeals and gate-knocking cases were sent back to the provincial authorities or memorialized to the ministry for escorted interrogation.

sentences.zh: 如情罪重大，以及事涉各省大吏，抑經言官、督撫彈劾，往往欽命大臣蒞審。

translations.literal: If circumstances and crime were grave, or the matter involved high officials of various provinces, or had been impeached by remonstrance officials or governors, often the emperor ordered a minister to preside at trial.
translations.idiomatic: Grave cases, matters involving provincial high officials, or cases impeached by censors or governors often drew an imperial order for a minister to preside.

sentences.zh: 發回及駮審之案，責成督撫率同司道親鞫，不準復發原問官，名為欽部事件。

translations.literal: Cases sent back or rejected for retrial were charged to the governor-general or governor to lead provincial judicial and circuit officials in personal interrogation, not permitted to send again to the original trial officer—called imperial-department cases.
translations.idiomatic: Sent-back and rejected cases were assigned to the governor or governor-general to interrogate personally with provincial officials, not to the original trial officer—these were called imperial-department cases.

sentences.zh: 文武官犯罪，題參革職。

translations.literal: When civil and military officials committed crimes, they were impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials who committed crimes were impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 道府、副將以上，遴委道員審理。

translations.literal: From circuit intendant and deputy commander upward, a circuit intendant was selected to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: From circuit intendant and deputy commander upward, a circuit intendant was appointed to try the case.

sentences.zh: 同知、游擊以下，遴委知府審理。

translations.literal: From subprefect and battalion commander downward, a prefect was selected to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: From subprefect and battalion commander downward, a prefect was appointed.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史，順治初猶常設。

translations.literal: Touring censors—in early Shunzhi they were still regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censors were still regularly established in early Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 四年，從大理寺卿王永吉奏，差官往直省恤刑，然皆不久停罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, following the memorial of Court of Revision chief Wang Yongji, officials were dispatched to the provinces for compassionate review of punishment, yet all were soon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, following Court of Revision chief Wang Yongji's memorial, officials were sent to the provinces for compassionate review, but the practice was soon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 外省刑名，遂總匯於按察使司，而督撫受成焉。

translations.literal: Outer-province criminal matters were then gathered under the provincial judicial commissioner's office, and governors-general and governors gave final approval.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial criminal matters were then consolidated under the provincial judicial commissioner, with governors giving final approval.

sentences.zh: 京師笞、杖及無關罪名詞訟，內城由步軍統領，外城由五城巡城御史完結，徒以上送部，重則奏交。

translations.literal: In the capital, rod and stick and lawsuits without criminal charges in the inner city were concluded by the Metropolitan Infantry Command, in the outer city by the Five-City patrol censors; penal servitude and above went to the ministry, grave cases were memorialized for submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, rod, stick, and non-criminal suits in the inner city fell to the Metropolitan Infantry Command; in the outer city to the Five-City patrol censors; penal servitude and above went to the ministry; grave cases were memorialized.

sentences.zh: 如非常大獄，或命王、大臣、大學士、九卿會訊。

translations.literal: For very great cases, princes, ministers, Grand Secretaries, or the Nine Ministers might be ordered to conduct joint interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Exceptionally grave cases might be assigned to princes, ministers, Grand Secretaries, or the Nine Ministers for joint interrogation.

sentences.zh: 自順治迄乾隆間，有御廷親鞫者。

translations.literal: From Shunzhi through Qianlong there were cases of personal interrogation in the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: From Shunzhi through Qianlong there were cases of personal interrogation before the throne.

sentences.zh: 律稱八議者犯罪，實封奏聞請旨，不許擅自句問。

translations.literal: The Code calls for the Eight Privileges: when such persons commit crimes, a sealed memorial is submitted to request instruction; unauthorized interrogation for execution is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Code's Eight Privileges required a sealed memorial before interrogation; unauthorized execution was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 在京大小官員亦如之。

translations.literal: Officials great and small in the capital were likewise treated.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials great and small were treated the same way.

sentences.zh: 若宗室有犯，宗人府會刑部審理。

translations.literal: If members of the imperial clan offended, the Imperial Clan Court joined the Ministry of Justice in trial.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen were tried jointly by the Imperial Clan Court and the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 覺羅，刑部會宗人府審理。

translations.literal: For Aisin Gioro, the Ministry of Justice joined the Imperial Clan Court in trial.
translations.idiomatic: Aisin Gioro were tried with the ministry joining the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 所犯笞、杖、枷號，照例折罰責打；

translations.literal: For offenses of rod, stick, or cangue, reduction and beating were applied according to regulation;
translations.idiomatic: Rod, stick, and cangue offenses were reduced and punished by beating according to regulation;

sentences.zh: 犯徒，宗人府拘禁；

translations.literal: for penal servitude, the Imperial Clan Court detained;
translations.idiomatic: penal servitude was served in Imperial Clan Court detention;

sentences.zh: 軍、流、鎖禁，俱照旗人折枷日期，滿日開釋。

translations.literal: military exile, banishment, and lockup all followed Banner reduction and cangue dates, released when the term was full.
translations.idiomatic: military exile, banishment, and lockup followed Banner cangue schedules and ended on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 屢犯軍、流，發盛京、吉林、黑龍江等處圈禁；

translations.literal: Repeated military exile or banishment sent one to confinement in circles at Shengjing, Jilin, Heilongjiang, and the like;
translations.idiomatic: Repeat military exiles and banished persons were confined in guarded compounds at Shengjing, Jilin, Heilongjiang, and elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 死刑，宗人府進黃冊。

translations.literal: capital punishment—the Imperial Clan Court submitted the yellow register.
translations.idiomatic: capital cases required a yellow register from the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 閹寺犯輕罪，內務府慎刑司訊決，徒以上亦送部。

translations.literal: Eunuchs who committed light crimes were tried and decided by the Internal Affairs Office's Cautious Punishment Bureau; penal servitude and above also went to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs guilty of light offenses were tried by the Internal Affairs Office's Cautious Punishment Bureau; penal servitude and above went to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 八旗地畝之訟，屬諸戶部現審處，刑事統歸刑部。

translations.literal: Lawsuits over Banner land belonged to the Ministry of Revenue's Current Review section; criminal matters were uniformly under the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Banner land disputes belonged to the Ministry of Revenue's Current Review section; criminal matters to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 清初有都統會審之制，有高牆拘禁之條，至乾隆時俱廢。

translations.literal: In early Qing there was joint trial by commanders-in-chief and the high-wall detention rule; by Qianlong both were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qing had joint trial by banner commanders and high-wall detention; both were abolished by Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 旗營駐防省分，額設理事同知。

translations.literal: In provinces with Banner garrisons, administrative subprefects for Banner affairs were established by quota.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces with Banner garrisons had quota posts of administrative subprefect for Banner affairs.

sentences.zh: 旗人獄訟，同知會同州縣審理。

translations.literal: Banner litigation was tried jointly by the subprefect and the local prefecture or county.
translations.idiomatic: Banner lawsuits were tried jointly by the subprefect and local civil officials.

sentences.zh: 熱河都統衙門特設理刑司，刑部派員聽訟，三年一任。

translations.literal: The Rehe commander's yamen specially established a Judicial Bureau; the Ministry of Justice dispatched officers to hear cases on three-year terms.
translations.idiomatic: The Rehe commander's yamen had a special Judicial Bureau with ministry officers on three-year terms.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，以吉林獄訟繁多，詔依熱河設立刑司例，令刑部揀派滿、漢郎中、員外、主事各一員，分別掌印主稿，統歸將軍管轄。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, because Jilin litigation was numerous, an edict followed the Rehe precedent to establish a criminal bureau; the ministry selected one Manchu and one Han director, vice director, and secretary each to hold seals and draft, all under the general's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3, because Jilin had excessive litigation, a criminal bureau was established on the Rehe model with paired Manchu and Han directors, vice directors, and secretaries from the ministry under the general.

sentences.zh: 嗣吉林建省裁撤，而熱河如故。

translations.literal: Later Jilin became a province and the bureau was abolished, while Rehe remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Jilin became a province the bureau was abolished; Rehe remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 蒙古刑獄，內外扎薩克王公、台吉、塔布囊及協理台吉等承審。

translations.literal: Mongol criminal matters were tried by inner and outer league princes, taiji, tabunang, and assistant taiji.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol criminal matters were tried by inner and outer league princes, taiji, tabunang, and assistant taiji.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十七年，曾遣內地官員教導蒙古王等聽斷盜案，後不常設。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi, inland officials were once dispatched to instruct Mongol princes in trying robbery cases; later this was not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 37 inland officials were once sent to instruct Mongol princes in robbery cases, but the practice was not kept up.

sentences.zh: 沿邊與民人交涉案件，會同地方官審理，死罪由盟長核報理籓院，會同三法司奏當。

translations.literal: Border cases involving interaction with civilians were tried jointly with local officials; capital crimes were reported by league chiefs to the Court of Colonial Affairs and jointly memorialized with the Three Judicial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Border cases involving civilians were tried with local officials; capital crimes were reported through league chiefs to the Court of Colonial Affairs and the Three Judicial Offices.

sentences.zh: 在京犯斬、絞，刑部審訖，會理籓院法司亦如之。

translations.literal: For decapitation and strangulation in the capital, after the ministry finished trial, the Court of Colonial Affairs and judicial offices joined likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Capital cases in the capital, after ministry trial, likewise involved the Court of Colonial Affairs and judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 盛京刑部掌讞盛京旗人及邊外蒙古之獄。

translations.literal: The Shengjing Ministry of Justice handled cases of Shengjing Banner people and Mongols beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Shengjing Ministry of Justice handled Shengjing Banner people and frontier Mongols.

sentences.zh: 秋審，會同四部侍郎、奉天府尹酌定實、緩匯題，蓋皆特別之制。

translations.literal: For autumn review, together with vice ministers of the four departments and the Fengtian prefect, deserving execution and deferral were weighed and memorialized—altogether special systems.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn review there joined four department vice ministers and the Fengtian prefect to classify cases—a special system.

sentences.zh: 凡檢驗，以宋宋慈所撰之洗冤錄為準，刑部題定驗屍圖格，頒行各省。

translations.literal: For all forensic examination, Song Ci's Washing Away of Wrongs was the standard; the ministry had fixed corpse-examination charts promulgated to all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Forensic examination followed Song Ci's Washing Away of Wrongs; the ministry's corpse-examination charts were promulgated to every province.

sentences.zh: 人命呈報到官，地方正印官隨帶刑書、仵作，立即親往相驗。

translations.literal: When a homicide was reported to the office, the local seal-holding official immediately took clerks and coroners to examine in person.
translations.idiomatic: When homicide was reported, the seal-holding official immediately took clerks and coroners to examine the body in person.

sentences.zh: 仵作據傷喝報部位之分寸，行兇之器物，傷痕之長短淺深，一一填入屍圖。

translations.literal: The coroner reported the inch-fraction of each wound site, the weapon used, and the length, depth, and shallowness of each wound, entering all into the corpse chart.
translations.idiomatic: The coroner reported wound locations by inch, weapons used, and dimensions of each wound on the corpse chart.

sentences.zh: 若屍親控告傷痕互異，許再行覆檢，不得違例三檢。

translations.literal: If the victim's kin complained that wounds differed, re-examination was permitted, but three examinations in violation of rule were not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: If the victim's kin disputed the wounds, re-examination was permitted, but a third examination was forbidden except by rule.

sentences.zh: 如自縊、溺水、事主被殺等案，屍屬呈請免驗者，聽。

translations.literal: In cases such as hanging, drowning, or the master killed, if the corpse's kin requested exemption from examination, it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In hanging, drowning, or master-killed cases, exemption from examination was permitted if the kin requested it.

sentences.zh: 京師內城正身旗人及香山等處各營房命案，由刑部當月司員往驗。

translations.literal: Capital homicides involving registered Banner people in the inner city and at Xiangshan and other camps were examined by the ministry's monthly duty officer.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-city homicides of registered Banner people and cases at Xiangshan and other camps were examined by the ministry's monthly duty officer.

sentences.zh: 街道及外城人命，無論旗、民，歸五城兵馬司指揮相驗。

translations.literal: Homicides on streets and in the outer city, whether Banner or civilian, were examined by the Five Cities' military patrol command.
translations.idiomatic: Street and outer-city homicides, Banner or civilian, were examined by the Five Cities military patrol.

sentences.zh: 檢驗不以實者有刑。

translations.literal: Those who examined without truth faced punishment.
translations.idiomatic: False examination was itself punishable.

sentences.zh: 凡訊囚用杖，每日不得過三十。

translations.literal: For interrogating prisoners with the stick, not more than thirty blows per day were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation with the stick was limited to thirty blows per day.

sentences.zh: 熱審得用掌嘴、跪鍊等刑，強盜人命酌用夾棍，婦人指，通不得過二次。

translations.literal: Summer review permitted slapping the mouth and kneeling in chains; robbery and homicide might use the leg-press at discretion; for women, finger-press—in all not more than twice.
translations.idiomatic: Summer review permitted slapping the mouth and kneeling in chains; robbery and homicide might use the leg-press; women received finger-press torture—not more than twice in all.

sentences.zh: 其餘一切非刑有禁。

translations.literal: All other non-statutory tortures were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: All other non-statutory tortures were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 斷罪必取輸服供詞，律雖有「眾證明白，即同獄成」之文，然非共犯有逃亡，並罪在軍、流以下，不輕用也。

translations.literal: Conviction had to obtain a confession of submission; though the Code has the text that when collective proof is clear it is the same as conviction completed, yet except for accomplices with fugitives and crimes below military exile, it was not lightly used.
translations.idiomatic: Conviction required a submitted confession; though the Code says clear collective proof equals conviction, this was not lightly applied except for accomplices with fugitives or crimes below military exile.

sentences.zh: 凡審限，直省尋常命案限六閱月，盜劫及情重命案、欽部事件並搶奪掘墳一切雜案俱定限四閱月。

translations.literal: As for trial time limits, in directly administered provinces ordinary homicide cases had a limit of six months; robbery, grave homicide, imperial-department cases, and all miscellaneous cases of robbery, grave digging, and the like had four months.
translations.idiomatic: Trial limits: ordinary homicide in the provinces, six months; robbery, grave homicide, imperial-department cases, and miscellaneous grave-robbing and robbery cases, four months.

sentences.zh: 其限六月者，州縣三月解府州，府州一月解司，司一月解督撫，督撫一月咨題。

translations.literal: For the six-month limit, prefecture and county had three months to send up to prefecture, prefecture one month to provincial judge, judge one month to governor, governor one month to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Under the six-month limit: county to prefecture in three months, prefecture to judge in one, judge to governor in one, governor to memorial in one.

sentences.zh: 其限四月者，州縣兩月解府州，府州二十日解司，司二十日解督撫，督撫二十日咨題。

translations.literal: For the four-month limit, prefecture and county had two months to prefecture, prefecture twenty days to judge, judge twenty days to governor, governor twenty days to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Under the four-month limit: county to prefecture in two months, prefecture to judge in twenty days, judge to governor in twenty days, governor to memorial in twenty days.

sentences.zh: 如案內正犯及要證未獲，或在監患病，准其展限或扣限。

translations.literal: If the principal offender or key witnesses in the case had not been captured, or if sick in prison, extension or deduction of the limit was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If the principal offender or key witnesses were still at large, or a prisoner was ill in custody, the deadline might be extended or suspended.

sentences.zh: 若隔屬提人及行查者，以人文到日起限。
