translations.literal: If persons were summoned across jurisdictions or investigations were sent out, the limit began from the day the person or report arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When prisoners were summoned across jurisdictions or inquiries dispatched, the clock started when the person or report arrived.

sentences.zh: 限滿不結，督撫咨部，即於限滿之日起算，再限二、三、四月，各級分限如前。

translations.literal: When the limit expired without conclusion, the governor memorialized the ministry; counting from the expiry date, another limit of two, three, or four months was set, with each level's division as before.
translations.idiomatic: If a case was not concluded when the limit expired, the governor reported to the ministry and a further two to four months was allowed, with the same tiered schedule.

sentences.zh: 如仍遲逾，照例參處。

translations.literal: If still delayed beyond that, impeachment followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Further delay brought impeachment under the regulations.

sentences.zh: 按察司自理事件，限一月完結。

translations.literal: Cases self-adjudicated by the provincial judicial commissioner had a one-month limit for conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Cases handled by the provincial judicial commissioner had to be concluded within one month.

sentences.zh: 州縣自理事件，限二十日審結。

translations.literal: Cases self-adjudicated by prefecture and county had a twenty-day limit for trial and conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: County and prefecture self-adjudicated cases had a twenty-day limit.

sentences.zh: 上司批發事件，限一月審報。

translations.literal: Cases dispatched by superiors had a one-month limit for trial and report.
translations.idiomatic: Cases assigned by superiors had to be tried and reported within one month.

sentences.zh: 刑部現審，笞杖限十日，遣、軍、流、徒二十日，命盜等案應會三法司者三十日。

translations.literal: For ministry current review: rod and stick, ten days; deportation, military exile, banishment, and penal servitude, twenty days; homicide and robbery requiring the Three Judicial Offices, thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry current review: rod and stick, ten days; deportation, military exile, banishment, and penal servitude, twenty days; homicides and robberies requiring the Three Offices, thirty days.

sentences.zh: 每月奏報，聲明曾否逾限。

translations.literal: Each month a memorial was submitted stating whether limits had been exceeded.
translations.idiomatic: Each month a report stated whether any limit had been exceeded.

sentences.zh: 如有患病及查傳等情，亦得依例扣展。

translations.literal: If there was illness or inquiry by dispatch and the like, deduction or extension was also permitted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Illness or pending inquiries also permitted suspension or extension under the rules.

sentences.zh: 速議速題，均限五日覆。

translations.literal: Rapid deliberation and rapid memorial all had a five-day limit for reply.
translations.idiomatic: Expedited deliberation and memorial required reply within five days.

sentences.zh: 死罪會核，自科鈔到部之日，立決限七十日，監候限八十日。

translations.literal: Joint verification of capital crimes—from the day the censorate copy reached the ministry, immediate execution seventy days, held awaiting eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: Capital joint review: from arrival of the censorate copy, seventy days for immediate execution, eighty for prisoners held awaiting.

sentences.zh: 會同題覆，院寺各分限八日。

translations.literal: Joint memorial for reply—the Court and Censorate each had an eight-day division.
translations.idiomatic: Joint reply memorials: eight days each for Court and Censorate.

sentences.zh: 由咨改題之案，展限十日。

translations.literal: Cases changed from report to memorial received a ten-day extension.
translations.idiomatic: Cases converted from routine report to memorial received ten extra days.

sentences.zh: 系清文加譯漢十日或二十日，逾限附參。

translations.literal: Those in Manchu with Chinese translation added ten or twenty days; exceeding the limit brought attached impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu documents requiring Chinese translation added ten or twenty days; overrun brought impeachment.

sentences.zh: 盜賊逾月不獲，捕役汛兵予笞，官罰俸。

translations.literal: If robbers were not captured within a month, constables and garrison soldiers were beaten with the rod and officials fined salary.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers not captured within a month brought rod punishment for constables and salary fines for officials.

sentences.zh: 吏兵兩部處分則例，尚有疏防及初、二、三、四參之分。

translations.literal: The Ministries of Civil and Military Affairs' disciplinary regulations also distinguished negligent defense and first through fourth impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military ministries' discipline regulations also distinguished negligent defense and degrees of impeachment.

sentences.zh: 命案兇犯在逃，承緝、接緝亦按限開參。

translations.literal: When the murderer in a homicide case escaped, initial pursuit and relay pursuit also opened impeachment according to limit.
translations.idiomatic: Escaped homicide suspects also triggered impeachment schedules for initial and relay pursuit.

sentences.zh: 然例雖嚴，而巧於規避者，蓋自若也。

translations.literal: Yet though the regulations were strict, those skilled at evasion remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though the rules were strict, those skilled at evasion carried on unchanged.

sentences.zh: 凡解犯有三：一、定案時之解審。

translations.literal: Escorting prisoners had three kinds: first, escort for trial at conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoner escort took three forms. First: escort for trial upon conviction.

sentences.zh: 徒犯解至府州轉報，軍、流、遣及死罪，自府州遞省，逐級訊問無異，督撫然後咨題。

translations.literal: Penal-servitude offenders were escorted to prefecture for transmission; military exile, banishment, deportation, and capital crimes from prefecture up through the province, examined at each level without discrepancy, then the governor memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Penal-servitude cases went to the prefecture; military exile, banishment, deportation, and capital crimes ascended through the province level by level, then the governor memorialized.

sentences.zh: 一、秋審時之解勘。

translations.literal: Second, escort for investigation at autumn review.
translations.idiomatic: Second: escort for autumn-review investigation.

sentences.zh: 死罪非立決，發回本州縣監禁，逮秋審，徑行解司審勘。

translations.literal: Capital crimes not immediately executed were sent back to prefecture and county for detention; when autumn review came, they were escorted directly to the provincial judge for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Non-immediate capital sentences returned to county detention, then at autumn review were escorted to the provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 官犯自定案即拘禁司監待決。

translations.literal: Official offenders from conviction were detained in the provincial prison awaiting decision.
translations.idiomatic: Official offenders were confined in the provincial prison from conviction onward.

sentences.zh: 常犯緩決者，二次秋審，即不復解。

translations.literal: Ordinary offenders with deferred decision were not escorted again after the second autumn review.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary deferred prisoners were not escorted again after their second autumn review.

sentences.zh: 其直省各邊地離督撫駐處窵遠，有由該管巡道審勘加結轉報者，非通例也。

translations.literal: In directly administered provinces with remote border districts far from the governor's seat, some were investigated by the touring circuit intendant with certification and transmission—not the general rule.
translations.idiomatic: Remote border districts sometimes used the circuit intendant for autumn investigation—not the general rule.

sentences.zh: 一、發遣時之解配。

translations.literal: Third, escort for assignment at dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Third: escort to place of punishment.

sentences.zh: 徒囚問發隔縣，軍、流起解省分，預行咨明應發省分督撫，查照道里表，酌量州縣大小遠近、在配軍流多寡，先期定地，飭知入境首站州縣，隨到隨發。

translations.literal: Penal-servitude offenders were assigned to counties in other jurisdictions; military exiles were dispatched from the sentencing province after prior notification to the receiving province's governor, who consulted the route table, weighed prefecture and county size, distance, and number of exiles already assigned, fixed the place in advance, and ordered the first county on entry to dispatch on arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude went to another county; military exiles required prior notice to the receiving province, which fixed the destination by route tables and local capacity.

sentences.zh: 遣犯解至例定地方安插。

translations.literal: Deportees were escorted to the place fixed by regulation for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: Deportees were escorted to their regulated place of resettlement.

sentences.zh: 犯籍州縣僉差，名曰長解。

translations.literal: The offender's home county selected escorts by contract, called long escort.
translations.idiomatic: The home county supplied contract escorts—the "long escort."

sentences.zh: 沿途州縣，派撥兵役護送，名為短解。

translations.literal: Along the route each county dispatched soldiers to guard and convey, called short escort.
translations.idiomatic: Each county along the route supplied soldiers—the "short escort."

sentences.zh: 罪囚視罪名輕重，定用鐵鎖杻釒道數。

translations.literal: Criminals were fitted with iron cangue, fetters, and chains according to the severity of the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fetters and chains were fitted according to the severity of the sentence.

sentences.zh: 若中途不覺失囚，訊明有無賄縱，分別治罪。

translations.literal: If a prisoner was lost en route without detection, whether there was bribery or release was investigated and punishment distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Lost prisoners en route were investigated for bribery or negligence and punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 隔屬關提及發交各地方官管束者，視此為差。

translations.literal: Summons across jurisdictions and delivery to local officials for supervision followed this with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-jurisdiction summons and delivery to local supervision followed similar rules.

sentences.zh: 京師現審，徒犯發順天府充徒。

translations.literal: For capital current review, penal-servitude offenders were sent to Shuntian prefecture for service.
translations.idiomatic: Capital penal-servitude offenders were assigned to Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 流囚由刑部定地，劄行順天府起送。

translations.literal: Exiled prisoners had their place fixed by the ministry, which notified Shuntian prefecture to dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles were assigned by the ministry, which ordered Shuntian to dispatch them.

sentences.zh: 五軍咨由兵部定地提發，外遣亦咨兵部差役起解。

translations.literal: The Five Armies reported through the Ministry of War for place assignment and dispatch; outer deportees also were escorted by Ministry of War runners.
translations.idiomatic: Five Armies cases went through the Ministry of War; outer deportees likewise.

sentences.zh: 綜計訴訟所歷，自始審迄終結，其程序各有定規，毋或逾越。

translations.literal: In sum, the course of litigation from first trial to final conclusion had fixed procedures at each stage, not to be overstepped.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, litigation from first hearing to final disposition followed fixed procedures at every stage.

sentences.zh: 迨光緒變法，三十二年，改刑部為法部，統一司法行政。

translations.literal: When Guangxu reforms came, in the thirty-second year the Ministry of Justice was changed to the Ministry of Law, unifying judicial administration.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 the Ministry of Justice became the Ministry of Law, centralizing judicial administration.

sentences.zh: 改大理寺為大理院，配置總檢察廳，專司審判。

translations.literal: The Court of Revision was changed to the Supreme Court, with a General Procuratorate attached, specializing in adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Revision became the Supreme Court with a General Procuratorate for adjudication.

sentences.zh: 於是法部不掌現審，各省刑名，畫歸大理院覆判，並不會都察院，而三法司之制廢。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Law no longer handled current review; provincial criminal cases were assigned to Supreme Court rejudgment, without the Censorate, and the Three Judicial Offices system was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry no longer tried cases; provincial criminal matters went to the Supreme Court without the Censorate, abolishing the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 題本改為摺奏，內閣無所事事。

translations.literal: Topic memorials became folded memorials; the Grand Secretariat had nothing to do.
translations.idiomatic: Routine memorials became folded submissions; the Grand Secretariat had little left to do.

sentences.zh: 秋、朝審專屬法部，其例緩者隨案聲明，不更加勘，而九卿、科道會審之制廢。

translations.literal: Autumn and court review belonged solely to the Ministry of Law; deferred cases were stated in the case itself without further investigation, and the Nine Ministers and censor joint review was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn and court review fell to the Ministry of Law; deferrals were noted in the case file, ending Nine Ministers and censor joint review.

sentences.zh: 京師暨各省設高等審檢廳，都城省會及商埠各設地方及初級審檢廳，改按察使為提法司。

translations.literal: High courts of trial and prosecution were established in the capital and provinces; local and primary courts in provincial capitals and commercial ports; the provincial judge became the procuratorial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: High and local courts of trial and prosecution were established; the provincial judge became procuratorial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，法部奏定各級廳試辦章程。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the Ministry of Law memorialized trial regulations for courts at each level.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 the ministry memorialized trial regulations for each court level.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，法律館奏頒法院編制法，由初級起訴之案不服，可控由地方而至高等，由地方起訴之案不服，可控由高等而至大理院，名為四級三審。

translations.literal: In Xuantong 2 the Law Codification Office memorialized the Court Organization Law: appeals from primary court went through local to high; from local court through high to Supreme Court—called four levels and three trials.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong 2 brought the Court Organization Law: primary to local to high to Supreme Court—four levels, three trials.

sentences.zh: 從前審級、審限、解審、解勘之制，州縣行之而不行於法院。

translations.literal: The former trial levels, limits, escort for trial, and escort for investigation applied at prefecture and county but not in the new courts.
translations.idiomatic: Former trial levels, deadlines, and escort rules applied to counties, not to the new courts.

sentences.zh: 審判分民事、刑事。

translations.literal: Trials were divided into civil and criminal.
translations.idiomatic: Trials were divided into civil and criminal.

sentences.zh: 民律艱於成書，所據者第舊律戶役、田宅、錢債、婚姻各條，而法未備。

translations.literal: The civil code was hard to complete; reliance was only on old-code household, land, debt, and marriage articles—and the law was incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: The civil code remained unfinished; courts relied on old household, land, debt, and marriage statutes—incomplete law.

sentences.zh: 司法事務有年度，判斷有評議，刑事有檢察官蒞審，人命由檢察官相驗，法院行之而不能行於州縣。

translations.literal: Judicial affairs had annual terms, judgments had deliberation, criminal cases had prosecutors at trial, homicides were examined by prosecutors—practiced in courts but not at prefecture and county.
translations.idiomatic: Courts had annual terms, deliberative judgments, prosecutorial attendance, and prosecutorial autopsy—unknown at the county level.

sentences.zh: 刑訴制度，蓋雜糅矣。

translations.literal: The criminal procedure system was altogether a hybrid.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal procedure had become a hybrid system.

sentences.zh: 然爾時所以急於改革者，亦曰取法東西列強，藉以收回領事裁判權也。

translations.literal: Yet the urgency of reform at that time was also said to be taking law from Western powers to recover consular jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Reform was also driven by the hope of modeling Western powers to recover consular jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 考領事裁判，行諸上海會審公堂，其源肇自咸豐朝，與英、法等國締結通商條約，約載中外商民交涉詞訟，各赴被告所屬之國官員處控告，各按本國律例審斷。

translations.literal: Examining consular jurisdiction, practiced at the Shanghai Mixed Court, it originated in the Xianfeng reign when commercial treaties with Britain, France, and others provided that in lawsuits between Chinese and foreigners each went to the defendant's national officials, each judging by its own law.
translations.idiomatic: Consular jurisdiction began in Xianfeng-era commercial treaties: Sino-foreign suits went to the defendant's national court under that nation's law—the Shanghai Mixed Court being the model.

sentences.zh: 嗣遇他國締約，俱援利益均霑之說，群相仿效。

translations.literal: Later when other states made treaties, all cited most-favored-nation clauses and imitated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Later treaty powers cited most-favored-nation clauses and followed suit.

sentences.zh: 同治八年，定有洋涇浜設官章程，遴委同知一員，會同各國領事審理華洋訴訟。

translations.literal: In Tongzhi 8 regulations were fixed for Yangjingbang officials; one subprefect was selected to join each nation's consul in trying Chinese-foreign suits.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi 8 fixed Yangjingbang regulations: one subprefect joined foreign consuls in mixed suits.

sentences.zh: 其外人應否科刑，讞員例不過問。

translations.literal: Whether foreigners should be punished—the Chinese judge by regulation did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Whether foreigners were punished—the Chinese judge did not inquire.

sentences.zh: 華人第限於錢債、鬥毆、竊盜等罪，在枷杖以下，准其決責。

translations.literal: Chinese were limited to money debts, brawls, theft, and crimes below rod and stick—these the court might punish.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese offenders in debts, brawls, and petty theft below rod and stick might be punished by the court.

sentences.zh: 後各領擴張權限，公堂有逕定監禁數年者。

translations.literal: Later each consul expanded authority; the mixed court sometimes fixed imprisonment for several years directly.
translations.idiomatic: Consuls later expanded powers; the mixed court sometimes imposed years of imprisonment directly.

sentences.zh: 外人不受中國之刑章，而華人反就外國之裁判。

translations.literal: Foreigners were not subject to China's penal code, while Chinese were judged under foreign courts.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners escaped Chinese law while Chinese were judged by foreign courts.

sentences.zh: 清季士大夫習知國際法者，每咎彼時議約諸臣不明外情，致使法權坐失。

translations.literal: Late-Qing scholars versed in international law often blamed the treaty negotiators of that time for not understanding foreign conditions, causing legal authority to be lost in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: Late-Qing scholars versed in international law blamed treaty negotiators for ignorance that cost China its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 光緒庚子以後，各國重立和約，我國齗齗爭令撤銷，而各使藉口中國法制未善，靳不之許。

translations.literal: After the Guangxu Gengzi treaties, nations renewed agreements; China strenuously demanded abolition, but ministers cited China's imperfect legal system and refused.
translations.idiomatic: After the Boxer treaties China demanded abolition; foreign ministers cited imperfect Chinese law and refused.

sentences.zh: 迨爭之既亟，始聲明異日如審判改良，允將領事裁判權廢棄。

translations.literal: When contention grew acute, they declared that if trials were reformed, consular jurisdiction would eventually be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Under pressure they promised eventual abolition if China's trials were reformed.

sentences.zh: 載在約章，存為左券。

translations.literal: This was recorded in the treaties and kept as proof on the left.
translations.idiomatic: This was written into treaties as a formal pledge.

sentences.zh: 故二十八年設立法律館，有「按照交涉情形，參酌各國法律，務期中外通行」之旨。

translations.literal: Therefore in the twenty-eighth year the Law Codification Office was established with the aim to "follow diplomatic circumstances, consult foreign laws, and ensure practice both inside and outside."
translations.idiomatic: Hence Guangxu 28 established the Law Codification Office to harmonize Chinese and foreign law.

sentences.zh: 蓋亦欲修明法律，俾外國就範也。

translations.literal: This was also to clarify law so foreigners would come within bounds.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was also to improve law so foreign powers would accept Chinese jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 夫外交視國勢之強弱，權利既失，豈口舌所能爭。

translations.literal: Diplomacy depends on national strength; once rights are lost, what can words dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Diplomacy follows national strength; lost rights cannot be recovered by argument alone.

sentences.zh: 故終日言變法，逮至國本已傷，而收效卒鮮，豈法制之咎與？

translations.literal: Therefore though reform was spoken of all day, by the time the national foundation was injured, results were still few—is this the fault of the legal system?
translations.idiomatic: Reform talk continued until the state was wounded, yet little was gained—was the legal system alone to blame?

sentences.zh: 然其中有變之稍善而未竟其功者，曰監獄。

translations.literal: Yet among changes, some were slightly better though not achieving full success: prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Some reforms improved matters without finishing the job—prisons among them.

sentences.zh: 有政體所關而未之變者，曰赦典。

translations.literal: Some concerned the polity itself and were not changed: amnesty statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Some touched the polity itself and went unchanged—amnesty.

sentences.zh: 監獄與刑制相消息，從前監羈罪犯，並無已決未決之分。

translations.literal: Prisons and the penal system are mutually responsive; formerly detained criminals had no distinction between decided and undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons and penal law interact; formerly there was no distinction between convicted and unconvicted detainees.

sentences.zh: 其囚禁在獄，大都未決犯為多。

translations.literal: Those imprisoned were mostly the undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Most prisoners were still awaiting trial.

sentences.zh: 既定罪，則笞、杖折責釋放，徒、流、軍、遣即日發配，久禁者斬、絞監候而已。

translations.literal: Once convicted, rod and stick were reduced and released; penal servitude, exile, military exile, and deportation were dispatched the same day; long confinement was only for decapitation and strangulation held awaiting.
translations.idiomatic: After conviction, rod and stick ended quickly; penal servitude and exile were dispatched at once; only capital prisoners awaiting review stayed long.

sentences.zh: 州縣監獄，以吏目、典史為管獄官，知州、知縣為有獄官，司監則設按司獄。

translations.literal: Prefecture and county prisons had the department clerk or archivist as prison officer and the prefect or magistrate as prison authority; provincial prisons had the judicial commissioner's jailer.
translations.idiomatic: County prisons were run by clerks under the magistrate; provincial prisons by the judicial commissioner's staff.

sentences.zh: 各監有內監以禁死囚，有外監以禁徒、流以下，婦人別置一室，曰女監。

translations.literal: Each prison had an inner ward for capital prisoners and an outer ward for penal servitude and below; women had a separate chamber called the women's prison.
translations.idiomatic: Prisons had inner wards for capital prisoners, outer wards for lesser sentences, and separate women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 徒以上鎖收，杖以下散禁。

translations.literal: Penal servitude and above were locked; rod and stick were held loosely.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude and above were locked; rod and stick offenders were loosely held.

sentences.zh: 囚犯日給倉米一升，寒給絮衣一件。

translations.literal: Prisoners received one sheng of granary rice daily; in cold weather one padded garment.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners received one sheng of rice daily and one padded garment in winter.

sentences.zh: 鎖杻常洗滌，席薦常鋪置，夏備涼漿，冬設暖床，疾病給醫藥。

translations.literal: Fetters were regularly washed; mats regularly laid; cool broth in summer, warm beds in winter; medicine when ill.
translations.idiomatic: Fetters were washed, bedding provided, cool drink in summer, warm beds in winter, medicine when ill.

sentences.zh: 然外省監獄多湫隘，故例有輕罪人犯及干連證佐，准取保候審之文。

translations.literal: Yet outer-province prisons were mostly cramped; hence the regulation permitting bail pending trial for light crimes and witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Outer-province prisons were cramped; regulations allowed bail for light crimes and witnesses.

sentences.zh: 無如州縣懼其延誤，每有班館差帶諸名目，胥役藉端虐詐，弊竇叢滋。

translations.literal: Yet prefectures and counties feared delay and used names like guard house and escort lodge; clerks and runners extorted under pretext, abuses multiplying.
translations.idiomatic: Yet magistrates feared delay and used guard houses and escort lodges; clerks extorted under countless pretexts.

sentences.zh: 雖屢經內外臣工參奏，不能革也。

translations.literal: Though repeatedly memorialized by officials inside and outside, it could not be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated memorials could not end the abuses.

sentences.zh: 刑部有南北兩監，額設司獄八員、提牢二員，掌管獄卒，稽查罪囚，輪流分值。

translations.literal: The ministry had North and South prisons with eight jail wardens and two chief jailers managing runners and inspecting prisoners on rotation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry's North and South prisons had eight wardens and two chief jailers on rotation.

sentences.zh: 每月派御史查監，有瘐斃者亦報御史相驗。

translations.literal: Each month a censor inspected the prison; if prisoners died of illness, the censor also examined the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly censorial inspection applied; deaths in custody were also examined.

sentences.zh: 年終並由部匯奏一次，防閒致為周備。

translations.literal: At year's end the ministry summarized and memorialized once; prevention was quite thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end ministry memorials made capital prevention relatively thorough.

sentences.zh: 自光緒三十二年審判畫歸大理院，院設看守所，以羈犯罪之待訊者，各級審檢廳亦然，於是法部犴狴空虛。

translations.literal: From Guangxu 32, when trial went to the Supreme Court, detention centers were set up for those awaiting trial at every level; the ministry's cells stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangxu 32 trials went to the Supreme Court, which set detention centers; the ministry's cells emptied.

sentences.zh: 別設已決監於外城，以容徒、流之工作，並令各省設置新監，其制大都采自日本。

translations.literal: A separate convicted prison was set up in the outer city for working penal servitude and exile; provinces were ordered to build new prisons, mostly modeled on Japan.
translations.idiomatic: A convicted prison outside the city held laboring prisoners; provinces built new prisons modeled on Japan.

sentences.zh: 監房有定式，工廠有定程。

translations.literal: Cells had fixed forms; workshops fixed schedules.
translations.idiomatic: Cells and workshops followed fixed standards.

sentences.zh: 法律館特派員赴東調查，又開監獄學堂，以備京、外新監之用。

translations.literal: The Law Codification Office sent officers to Japan to investigate and opened a prison school for capital and provincial use.
translations.idiomatic: The Law Codification Office studied Japanese prisons and opened a prison school.

sentences.zh: 然斯時新法初行，措置未備，外省又限於財力，未能遍設也。

translations.literal: Yet the new law had just begun and arrangements were incomplete; outer provinces, limited by finances, could not build everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: New law was not yet complete and provinces lacked funds to build everywhere.

sentences.zh: 赦典有恩赦、恩旨之別。

translations.literal: Amnesty statutes distinguished general amnesty from imperial grace edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty distinguished general amnesty from grace edicts.

sentences.zh: 歷朝登極、升祔、冊立皇后、皇上五旬以上萬壽、皇太后六旬以上萬壽及武功克捷之類，例有恩赦。

translations.literal: Each reign's accession, spirit tablet elevation, empress investiture, imperial birthday above fifty, empress dowager birthday above sixty, and military victories customarily brought general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Accessions, spirit elevations, empress investitures, imperial birthdays above fifty, empress dowager birthdays above sixty, and military victories customarily brought general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 其詔書內開：一、官吏軍民人等有犯，除謀反、大逆、子孫謀殺祖父母父母、內亂、妻妾殺夫、奴婢殺家長、殺一家非死罪三人、採生折割人、謀殺故殺真正人命、蠱毒魘魅毒藥殺人、強盜、妖言、十惡等真正死罪不赦外，軍務獲罪、隱匿逃人及侵貪入己亦不赦外，其餘已發覺未發覺、已結未結者，咸赦除之。

translations.literal: The edict opened: officials, soldiers, and commoners who committed crimes—except true capital crimes of treason, great sedition, children plotting to kill grandparents or parents, internal disorder, wife or concubine killing husband, slave killing master, killing three in one household not capital crimes, cutting living persons for medicine, plotting or intentional killing of true human life, witchcraft and poison murder, robbery, sedition, the ten abominations and the like, also except military offenses, concealing fugitives, and embezzlement for personal gain—whether discovered or not, concluded or not, all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts listed capital exceptions—treason, parricide, sedition, witchcraft, robbery, the ten abominations, military crimes, fugitive concealment, embezzlement—then pardoned the rest, discovered or not, concluded or not.

sentences.zh: 若尋常萬壽及喜慶等事，則傳旨行赦。

translations.literal: For ordinary birthdays and celebrations, grace was conveyed by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary birthdays and celebrations received grace by edict only.

sentences.zh: 恩赦死罪以下俱免，恩旨則死罪已下遞減。

translations.literal: General amnesty exempted all below capital crime; grace edicts reduced capital and below by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: General amnesty freed all below capital crime; grace edicts reduced sentences by degree.

sentences.zh: 詔書既頒，刑部檢查成案，分別准免不準免，開單奏定，名為恩赦條款。

translations.literal: Once the edict was promulgated, the ministry checked cases, distinguishing permitted and not permitted exemption, memorializing the list as amnesty articles.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry then checked cases into permitted and denied lists—amnesty articles.

sentences.zh: 恩旨則分別准減不準減，名為減等條款。

translations.literal: Grace edicts distinguished permitted and denied reduction—reduction articles.
translations.idiomatic: Grace edicts produced reduction articles for permitted and denied reductions.

sentences.zh: 部設減等處，專司核駮。

translations.literal: The ministry established a Reduction Bureau specializing in verification.
translations.idiomatic: A Reduction Bureau specialized in verification.

sentences.zh: 其巡幸所經，赦及一方，及水旱兵災、清理庶獄者，則視詔旨從事焉。

translations.literal: Where the emperor toured, amnesty reached one region; for flood, drought, war, or clearing crowded prisons, the edict was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Touring amnesty covered one region; disasters and prison clearances followed the edict's terms.

sentences.zh: 明制，徒、流已至配，不復援赦。

translations.literal: Under the Ming system, once penal servitude or exile reached assignment, amnesty was not invoked.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming law, assigned penal servitude and exile were not amnestied.

sentences.zh: 清自康熙九年准在配徒犯會赦放免。

translations.literal: From Kangxi 9, assigned penal-servitude offenders might join general amnesty for release.
translations.idiomatic: From Kangxi 9 assigned penal-servitude offenders might be amnestied.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年恩詔，軍、流在配三年，安靜悔過，情原回籍，查明准釋。

translations.literal: Qianlong 2 grace edict: military exiles assigned three years, if quiet and repentant, might return home when investigated and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 2 allowed military exiles after three years of quiet conduct to return home if approved.

sentences.zh: 迨嘉慶二十五年，始將到配未及三年人犯一體查辦，尤為曠典。

translations.literal: By the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing, those who had reached assignment but not yet three years were all investigated and handled together—especially an empty precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Jiaqing 25 were prisoners who had reached their place of assignment but served less than three years included in general review—a precedent widely regarded as excessive.

sentences.zh: 昔人有言：「赦者小人之幸，君子之不幸。」

translations.literal: A man of old said: "Amnesty is the petty man's fortune and the gentleman's misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Someone of old remarked: "Amnesty is the fortune of the petty man and the misfortune of the gentleman."

sentences.zh: 意第謂赦恩之不可濫耳。

translations.literal: The meaning is only that amnesty grace must not be abused.
translations.idiomatic: The point was simply that amnesty must not be abused.

sentences.zh: 若夫非常慶典，特頒汗號，使之蕩滌瑕穢，洒然自新，未始非仁政之一端。

translations.literal: As for extraordinary celebrations, specially issuing broad pardon, enabling them to wash away stains and faults and renew themselves with ease—this is not without being one aspect of humane government.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on extraordinary occasions, when a broad pardon allowed offenders to wash away their stains and begin anew, that too was not without its place in humane government.

sentences.zh: 有清一代，赦典屢頒，然條款頗嚴，毋虞濫及。

translations.literal: Throughout the Qing dynasty, amnesty statutes were frequently promulgated, yet the articles were quite strict, without worry of excessive extension.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Qing, amnesties were frequent, but the articles were strict enough that abuse was seldom a concern.

sentences.zh: 且行慶施惠，王者馭世之大權，非苟然也。

translations.literal: Moreover, performing celebration and bestowing grace is the great authority by which a king governs the age—not something done carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Celebration and grace were among the great prerogatives by which a ruler governed the realm—not matters undertaken lightly.

sentences.zh: 故光緒三十四年宣統登極，猶循例大赦雲。

translations.literal: Therefore in the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu, when Xuantong ascended the throne, they still followed precedent in a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even in Guangxu 34, when Xuantong ascended the throne, a great amnesty was still proclaimed according to precedent.
